To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rapid decline of HCG levels to negative levels by week 2 of PI triple therapy was associated with SVR, while the persistence of viraemia (HCV RNA and/or HCV antigen positivity) at week 4 was associated with treatment failure.

the HCV antigen test is a useful marker for predicting SVR during the first 4 weeks of PI-based triple therapies and may be considered as a useful alternative for monitoring treatment responses to DAAs.

(1) HCV antigen testing is a useful tool for monitoring virological responses to HCV protease inhibitor therapy, (2) HCV antigen levels are a useful predictor of sustained virological responses in HCV patients treated with protease inhibitors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel diagnostic tests for the rapid diagnosis of HCV and the monitoring of treatment response to antiviral therapy.
the development of a novel, rapid and inexpensive test for the early prediction of treatment outcome in HCV patients.
the potential of HCV core antigen as a predictor of treatment outcome in the PI era.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although HCV antigen testing is not a substitute for viral load monitoring, it may be a useful adjunct to guide therapy and reduce the need for frequent viral RNA measurements.
HCV antigen testing may have a potential role in monitoring viral kinetics and guiding treatment decisions during DAA-based therapies.
, in the context of the new DAAs, HCV core antigen measurement may be considered for use as an alternative to RNA measurement to monitor virological response in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HCV Core Antigen assay is a valuable tool in the management of HCV infection and can be used to monitor the early virological kinetics of patients receiving PI-based therapy.
HCV core antigen testing can be considered as a useful tool for monitoring virological treatment response in the PI era.
HCV core antigen measurement may be a valuable addition to current monitoring strategies for patients undergoing PI triple therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rapid decline in HCV antigen level to negative level at 2 weeks of PI therapy is a predictor of SVR.
HCV antigen testing may be used in monitoring the early viral kinetics during PI triple therapy, which may have a role in guiding the treatment duration and/or the need for dose adjustment.
the rapid clearance of HCV core antigen in the first 2 weeks of therapy is a good predictor of SVR in patients treated with PI-based triple therapy.
